ns2:section.sectionText: This course will be offered online via BTAA CourseShare utilizing Zoom and Canvas. Instructor: Prof. Russell Burge at Indiana University. This graduate seminar offers an introduction to themes and debates in modern Korean history, beginning with the late Chosŏn period and working through colonial occupation, national division, and the divergent histories of North and South Korea. Drawing from both classic as well as newer English-language works, this course will familiarize students with debates on Korean history concerning topics as varied as war, identity formation, knowledge production, and protest. In addition to synthesizing the contributions of the writers under discussion, we will also explore the limitations of the field as well as its possible futures.
